excluded.label: decorates
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — the csharp-annotation precedent: an annotation is PASSIVE METADATA a tool reads, and a decorator is an APPLIED CALLABLE; a `decorates` row for a MATLAB attribute list would assert an application the vocabulary does not credit). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND ITS RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the vendored grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json) carries 148 node types of which 76 are named, and 0 of the 76 is a decorator/annotation production that wraps or applies to a declaration; the grammar DOES carry `attribute` and `attributes` (2 of the 76 named types), and those are exactly the class the adjudicated ontology holds to be passive metadata — a parenthesised ACCESS-SPECIFICATION list (`properties (SetAccess=private)`, `methods (Static)`) that the runtime reads off the declaration, never a callable applied to it. R3 (express on an existing node type) therefore EXISTS on `attributes` and is NOT TAKEN for the ONTOLOGICAL reason, never for difficulty. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (admitted files [0,3) of 3, transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): attributes lists 0, attribute entries 0, distinct attribute spellings 0. THE DOABILITY HALF IS PINNED ELSEWHERE, NOT LOST: the fixture validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/class-surface.m exercises `properties (SetAccess=private)` and `methods (Access=private)` and the analyzer publishes the resulting VISIBILITY on the property/method symbols rather than inventing a relationship. FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): (1) a decorator/annotation production in the SERVED grammar that APPLIES to a declaration — counted 0 of the 76 named node types; the census line turning non-zero refutes the ruling; (2) an attribute site in the admitted population whose attribute is invoked as a callable applied to the declaration — counted 0 of 0 attribute sites in 0 of 3 files.

excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — MATLAB has no markup/component template construct, and the only component-shaped model it has is App Designer, whose UI is a CONTAINER TREE OF WIDGET CONSTRUCTOR CALLS inside a `.mlapp` archive, not a component symbol a file-scoped analyzer can render). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND THE RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the served grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json, 148 node types / 76 named) carries 0 render/component/template/markup/widget production, so a grammar patch could not be built from the language; R3 could express `uifigure(...)`/`uicontrol(...)` as ordinary `function_call` nodes (the construct IS a call), and R3 is NOT TAKEN because the edge it would publish has NO VALID TARGET: the contract is 'a component RENDERS another component', and a UI widget constructor's first argument is a PARENT CONTAINER object or a name/value list, not a declared component symbol. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): UI component constructor calls 0 (0 of the 23 widget constructor spellings appear); `.mlapp` files on the corpus tree 0 — and a `.mlapp` is a ZIP archive the ROUTER admits to no lane, so the App Designer route does not reach this lane's population either. FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): a UI constructor call whose first argument is an IDENTIFIER naming a DECLARED component symbol — counted 0 of 0 constructor sites; or a served-grammar production that carries a rendered-component reference — counted 0 of the 76 named node types. The `.mlapp` count turning non-zero on the corpus tree would also reopen the question, and the census prints it.

excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — MATLAB has no mixin/trait/composition clause; its only multi-parent construct is the SUPERCLASS LIST, and every base in it is an IS-A base whose members are INHERITED). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND ITS RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the served grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json, 148 node types / 76 named) carries `superclasses` (with `<` and `&`) as the inheritance production and 0 mixin/with/trait/include/composition production; a grammar patch would have to INVENT a construct MATLAB does not have. R3 exists — the `&` sites are ordinary `superclasses` children — and R3 is NOT TAKEN because the relation it would publish is a DIFFERENT relation from the one measured: a base named after `&` is still a superclass (the class IS-A it, and `isa()` answers true), so the analyzer publishes it as `implements` (additional superclass conformance), never as member-set composition. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): classes with a superclasses node 0, classes with TWO OR MORE bases (`&` sites) 0, superclass entries 0. THE CONSTRUCT IS PINNED BY FIXTURES: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/class-and-methods.m pins `classdef Report < BaseReport` as `extends`, and validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/heritage.m pins `classdef Multi < BaseOne & BaseTwo & matlab.mixin.Copyable` as one extends plus two implements. FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): (1) a grammar production that composes a class from another class's member set WITHOUT an IS-A base — counted 0 of the 76 named node types; (2) a `classdef X < Y & Z` site where a base is NOT an IS-A superclass — counted 0 of 0 superclass entries over the population. A single such site refutes the ruling.

decisions.question: The population the gate admits for matlab is 3 `.m` files, all Objective-C by content (the router's `function ` substring matches English prose in comments). Should the lane measure them, exclude them, or report the router defect and stop?
decisions.answer: MEASURE THEM AND DISCLOSE. Production routes these files to the MATLAB grammar, so they ARE the lane's population; replacing or filtering them would be a workaround that makes the lane's denominator disagree with production's. Every count in this spec is over that population, `_population` states the content fact with the three trigger lines, and the fixture suite carries the doability evidence for the types the population cannot exercise. The routing defect itself is reported to the Lead (it is production code, not the analyzer).
decisions.pinnedBy: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/census-constructs.ts + validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt (admitted 3, tracked 412 = 3 + 153 absent + 256 routed to objective-c), and the incoming gate's own line `corpus has 3 .m files across 2 repos`

decisions.question: Is `classdef X < Y & Z` one inheritance relation or a conformance list — and which label does each base get?
decisions.answer: THE FIRST BASE IS extends, EVERY FOLLOWING BASE IS implements. MATLAB has a single inheritance clause whose list admits several superclasses; the first base is the class's primary IS-A relation, and each additional base is conformance to one more superclass. `mixes_in` is wrong for it: a base named after `&` is an IS-A base whose members are inherited, not a composed member set — the ruling in `excluded` carries that distinction with its counts.
decisions.pinnedBy: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/heritage.m (fires both, forbids the inversions and dotted-base splitting)

decisions.question: MATLAB has no module symbol; is `exports` expressible, or is every row X -> X and therefore informational?
decisions.answer: EXPRESSIBLE WHERE IT IS INFORMATIVE. The file IS the module and its module name is the package-qualified basename; for a `+pkg/` file that name differs from the exported declaration's leaf name, so the row is informative and is published. For a flat file the module name equals the declaration name (MATLAB's `foo.m`/`foo` identity) and the row would be X -> X, so it is WITHHELD by design rather than published as noise. The withhold is pinned as a forbid row, and the population count (0 top-level declarations) is printed.

decisions.question: Is a `+pkg/` folder membership a `part_of`, given there is no inclusion directive anywhere in the language?
decisions.answer: YES, and it is the lane's most interesting construct: MATLAB's namespace mechanism is a FOLDER, so the membership fact exists only in the file path the engine hands the analyzer. A declaration in `+pkg/f.m` is a PART of the `mypkg` package (`partRole: part`), and nested `+a/+b/f.m` is package `a.b`. The row is derived from the path, never from text, and its target is a symbol-shaped package name.
decisions.pinnedBy: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/+mypkg/pkgfunc.m (fires the part_of row; forbids a path segment outside the package as the target)
